text: gene-protein pair, method proceeds two stages: Stage 1 (within-donor): donor \(d\) least min_cells cells specified cell type, compute Spearman partial correlation gene expression protein abundance, controlling library sizes user-specified confounders: $$r_d = \rho_S(\text{gene}_i, \text{protein}_j \mid   \text{nCount\_RNA}, \text{nCount\_protein},   \text{confounders})$$ apply Fisher's z-transform: $$z_d = \text{arctanh}(r_d), \quad   \text{Var}(z_d) \approx 1.06 / (n_d - q - 3)$$ \(q\) number conditioning variables (2 + length confounders, less constant within donor therefore dropped). factor 1.06 corrects efficiency loss rank-based correlation (Fieller et al. 1957). Stage 2 (across-donor meta-regression): Fit random-effects model via REML Knapp-Hartung adjustment: $$z_d = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{exposure}_d   + \sum_k \gamma_k \cdot \text{moderator}_{dk}   + u_d + \varepsilon_d$$ \(\varepsilon_d \sim N(0, v_d)\) (known sampling variance) \(u_d \sim N(0, \tau^2)\) (-donor heterogeneity). Knapp-Hartung adjustment provides accurate confidence intervals small numbers studies (donors), using t-distribution \(D - p - 1\) degrees freedom rather z-distribution. Confounder control: Cell-level confounders (cell cycle, mitochondrial content, ambient RNA scores) partialed Stage 1, ensuring correlation reflects genuine gene-protein coupling rather shared technical biological confounds. Donor-level moderators (age, sex) included Stage 2.
